Metric Description: OpenFactCheck is an open-source toolkit that makes it easier to fact-check LLM outputs in a consistent, modular way.

FreshQA is a continually updated benchmark that tests whether LLMs can answer current, fast-changing questions and debunk false premises, showing today’s models often fail on both and that a simple retrieval-augmented prompt (FreshPrompt) can improve correctness while reducing hallucinations.
BLEU scores a generated text by measuring how much its word sequences (n-grams) overlap with one or more reference texts, with a penalty for overly short outputs.
BERTScore measures how similar a generated text is to a reference by comparing the meanings of their words using BERT embeddings, and reports precision, recall, and F1.
QAFactEval checks whether a summary is factually consistent by asking and answering questions about it, and it improves reliability by generating better questions and filtering out unanswerable ones.

RealTime QA is a benchmark that is updated weekly that tests whether systems can answer questions about newly emerging events, showing retrieval helps models stay current but they still give outdated answers when evidence is missing.

The Intraclass Correlation Coefficient (ICC) quantifies how consistently repeated measurements (e.g., multiple runs on the same inputs) agree with each other, with higher ICC indicating greater reproducibility.

CheckList is a testing method that checks robustness by making small, controlled changes to an input (like typos or harmless wording edits) and seeing whether the model still gives the right kind of answer.

SYCON Bench operationalizes conversational sycophancy as a model’s susceptibility to user pressure by quantifying the latency to the first stance change (“flip”) and the total number of stance changes across a controlled multi-turn interaction.
StableToolBench quantifies whether an LLM agent can successfully and consistently use external tools/APIs to complete tasks, while controlling for failures caused by unstable real-world endpoints.
The System Usability Scale (SUS) is a short 10-item post-use questionnaire that produces a single overall usability score (0–100) reflecting users’ perceived ease of use.
OpeNLGauge is a reference-free, LLM-based metric that rates generated text on qualities like fluency and can point to specific parts of the output that explain the score.

StructEval evaluates how reliably an LLM can produce machine-executable structured outputs, especially code and other rigid, parser-checked formats, by scoring whether generations satisfy strict structural/validation constraints.

FOFO evaluates how reliably an LLM can follow human-facing formatting instructions, like templates, layouts, and presentation rules, by measuring whether outputs match the required readable, user-specified format rather than executable code.
AIS quantifies what fraction of a model’s output can be directly traced to, and supported by, the provided source documents.

REVEAL is a benchmark dataset for verifying chain-of-thought reasoning that provides step-level labels indicating whether each reasoning step is relevant, supported by evidence, and logically correct.

NVIDIA operationalizes LLM infrastructure cost as total cost of ownership (TCO) for inference, combining the end-to-end serving stack costs (e.g., GPU hardware/instances plus supporting system costs) and often reporting it as an amortized cost per unit of inference work (e.g., per token or per throughput level).

TokenPowerBench is a benchmarking framework for systematically measuring and analyzing the power consumption and energy efficiency of large language model inference across different models, hardware, and configurations to help optimize costs and sustainability.
CEBench evaluates LLM pipelines by converting their measured compute usage into an estimated $ cost per run, so you can compare performance against real operational cost.

Metric: Time to First Token (TTFT) and Inter-token Latency (ITL)
Metric Description: Time to First Token (TTFT) measures the delay from request start to the first generated token, while Inter-Token Latency (ITL) measures the time between subsequent tokens during decoding, and together they capture both the startup latency and the streaming generation speed needed to evaluate LLM responsiveness.

Smooth Goodput measures how many LLM requests per second meet streaming latency targets in a way that reflects real user experience, without being inflated by tricks like delaying tokens or dropping slow requests.

JailBreakV introduces a large-scale benchmark that tests multimodal LLM safety by measuring how well text- and image-based jailbreak attacks (including transfers from LLM jailbreaks) can bypass safeguards, typically reported via Attack Success Rate (ASR) across diverse adversarial scenarios.

SORRY-Bench is a balanced, fine-grained benchmark that measures an LLM’s safety-refusal behavior by testing whether it refuses vs. fulfills unsafe instructions across 44–45 unsafe topic categories and diverse prompt augmentations, with human annotations and an efficient automated evaluator to score refusals.

HarmMetric introduces a benchmark dataset and scoring framework for evaluating harmfulness metrics and LLM-based judges on harmful prompts paired with diverse harmful/non-harmful responses, and it finds that simple overlap metrics like METEOR and ROUGE-1 can outperform LLM judges at assessing harmfulness.

RealToxicityPrompts measures a model’s tendency to generate toxic language by having it continue naturally occurring prompts and scoring the generations with the Perspective API toxicity score, typically reported as mean toxicity and/or the rate of outputs above a toxicity threshold.

KL-extractability (as used in practice) measures verbatim memorization by prompting a model with a prefix from a target sequence and scoring how many tokens of the true continuation the model reproduces under greedy decoding

PII-Scope introduces a benchmark and evaluation framework for measuring training-data PII leakage in LLMs by running standardized PII extraction attacks across multiple threat settings and reporting extraction/leakage effectiveness (e.g., success rates) by PII type.

PersistBench is a benchmark for memory-enabled LLM assistants that tests whether stored memories are used appropriately over time, measuring failure cases like cross-domain leakage (irrelevant memories showing up in answers) and reporting how often they happen.
